question.text: Which type of platform facilitates transactions in Direct Plans of mutual funds for investors?

answer.text: A bank acting as a corporate distributor with ARN
An individual financial advisor with ARN and EUIN
An Execution Only Platform (EOP) such as Kuvera or Groww in direct-plan mode
An NBFC distributing mutual funds through its branch network

explanation.text: The Logic: Execution Only Platforms (EOPs) such as Kuvera and Groww (in direct-plan mode) facilitate transactions in Direct Plans of mutual funds. The NISM Series V-A workbook (p.73, p.120) describes EOPs as new-age platforms through which investors can buy Direct Plans, since Direct Plans are designed for investors purchasing units directly from the fund without routing through a traditional distributor. The Trap: Options A, B, and D all involve ARN-holding distributors. Per p.308, MFDs (Mutual Fund Distributors) typically deal in Regular Plans because their trail commission is embedded in the Regular Plan TER. The differentiating concept the exam tests is the EOP route as a non-ARN-distributor channel for Direct Plans. Note: Direct Plans have a lower TER than Regular Plans because no distributor commission is embedded. The source describes EOPs as a recognized channel for Direct Plan transactions, alongside investors transacting directly with the AMC.
